texts.li: {A_nameDef} hummed the same four notes all afternoon at work, and {B_nameDef}, a few paces off, finally threw down {B_possessive} tools and asked whether {A_pronoun} knew any others.
{B_nameDef} asked {A_nameDef} to stop humming. {A_nameDef} said {A_pronoun} wasn't. {A_nameDef} was.
{B_nameDef} has started working at the far end of the room, as far from {A_nameDef}'s humming as the walls allow.
{B_nameDef} started humming along with {A_nameDef} at work, badly, and they finished the job as a duet.
{B_nameDef} caught {A_nameDef}'s tune and couldn't get rid of it all day. By evening they were both humming it.

ColonyCouncil.SocialEventDef.label: words spoken in sleep

texts.li: At breakfast {B_nameDef} repeated, word for word, what {A_nameDef} had said in {A_possessive} sleep. {A_nameDef} wanted to know how {B_nameDef} had come to hear it.
{B_nameDef} told the table that {A_nameDef} argues with someone called Vera in {A_possessive} sleep, and loses. {A_nameDef} didn't think it was funny.

ColonyCouncil.SocialEventDef.note: told what was said in sleep

texts.li: {A_nameDef} was up before dawn and cheerful about it, and said so to {B_nameDef}, who had gone to bed an hour before.
{A_nameDef} asked {B_nameDef} at noon whether {B_pronoun} was only just up. {B_nameDef} asked {A_nameDef} whether {A_pronoun} ever stopped talking about mornings.
{B_nameDef} has taken to eating in the kitchen doorway, because {A_nameDef} sings while {A_pronoun} cooks, and the food tastes better for it, {B_nameDef} says.
{B_nameDef} asked {A_nameDef} for the song along with the recipe. {A_nameDef} said they only work together.
{A_nameDef} cleared {B_nameDef}'s things off the table while {B_nameDef} was still using them, and stacked them very neatly somewhere {B_nameDef} couldn't find.
{B_nameDef} left a cup on the table for a moment. When {B_pronoun} came back {A_nameDef} had washed it, dried it and put it away, and was waiting to say something about it.
{A_nameDef} gave {B_nameDef} a little carved bird, made out of an offcut over a few evenings. {B_nameDef} has put it by {B_possessive} bed.
{A_nameDef} had been whittling something for days without saying what. It turned out to be for {B_nameDef}: a small, careful likeness of {B_possessive} favourite animal.
{A_nameDef} remembered that today was the day {B_nameDef} first came to the colony, and was the only one who did. {B_nameDef} was more touched than {B_pronoun} let on.
{A_nameDef} wished {B_nameDef} well for a day that mattered to {B_objective}, and {B_nameDef} had no idea anyone knew.
{A_nameDef} took {B_nameDef} out past the lamps last night and named the stars for {B_objective}, one by one. {B_nameDef} suspects {A_nameDef} made half of them up.
{B_nameDef} found {A_nameDef} lying on the cold ground looking up, and lay down beside {A_objective}. They stayed until the dew came.
{A_nameDef} counted the steps to the storeroom out loud while {B_nameDef} was trying to think, and then counted them again on the way back.
{B_nameDef} lost {B_possessive} place three times because {A_nameDef} was counting something under {A_possessive} breath. {B_nameDef} asked what. {A_nameDef} said it was best not to stop now.
{A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} have discovered they are both superstitious, and spent the evening comparing notes and topping up each other's precautions.
{B_nameDef} caught {A_nameDef} at {A_possessive} little ritual and, instead of laughing, showed {A_objective} {B_possessive} own.
{A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} argued for an hour over what to name the newest animal in the pens. They settled on two names, and use one each.
{A_nameDef} has given every animal in the colony a name. {B_nameDef}, who looks after them, has started using them, and pretends it was {B_possessive} idea.
